laws.rule: Liquor, Gaming and Cannabis Control Act, C.C.S.M. c. L153, s. 57(1): except where the Act allows it, nobody may drink liquor in a public place or hold liquor there that is in an opened or unsealed container, or out of its original container. Liquor may otherwise be drunk only in a residence, licensed premises or a private place as defined in the regulations (s. 57(2)), and the Act and regulations allow some exceptions (s. 57(3)).

The legal drinking age in Manitoba is 19: a minor (under 19) may not possess or drink liquor, except as the Act permits (s. 63). A parent, guardian or spouse may give liquor to a minor in a residence (s. 62), and a minor may attend a social occasion but may not drink or hold liquor there. Showing altered, borrowed or forged ID to buy liquor or enter licensed premises is an offence (s. 64).

Nobody may drive, or have care and control of, a motor vehicle, moving or not, with liquor in it unless the vehicle is licensed or permitted (s. 60(1)). Exceptions: liquor in unopened or unsealed containers; liquor in the trunk, an outside compartment or other space not readily accessible to people in the vehicle; in a station wagon, van or hatchback, liquor behind the rear of the last seat; and, for a motor home, liquor in a cabinet away from the driver's area or while it is used as a residence (s. 60(2)).

Under the same Act, cannabis must be in its federal packaging, labelled and stamped (s. 101.15.2), and nobody may operate or have care and control of a boat with cannabis in it unless it is kept in a closed compartment (s. 101.26). The Act sets 19 as the age: young persons (under 19) may not possess or consume cannabis (s. 101.18), and showing ID that is altered or not lawfully issued to buy cannabis is an offence (s. 101.19).

items.text: The legal age for cannabis in Manitoba is 19. Adults may carry up to 30 g of dried cannabis (or equivalent) in public, and buy only from retailers licensed by the Liquor, Gaming and Cannabis Authority of Manitoba, in person or online.

Smoking or vaping cannabis is illegal in all public places, including streets and sidewalks, parks and beaches (provincial parks too), school grounds, restaurant patios and decks, the grounds of health-care facilities, and enclosed public places.

In a vehicle, cannabis must be stowed in the trunk or another space not readily reachable by anyone inside. The province lists preset fines of C$237 (about A$241) for carrying improperly stored cannabis and C$672 (about A$683) for using cannabis in a vehicle on a highway or in an off-road vehicle, at the RBA rate of 30 October 2026, A$1 = CAD 0.9838.

Since 1 May 2025 adults 19 and over may grow up to four cannabis plants at home (four per household), indoors and out of reach of young people. Some older provincial pages still say home growing is banned.
The legal drinking age in Manitoba is 18, and anyone who looks close to that age must show valid photo ID.
The Liquor, Gaming and Cannabis Control Act bans drinking liquor, or having open liquor, in a public place (s. 57).
